subject: Production incident: elevated tail latency and request queuing
messages:
From: Michael Carter <michael.carter@peregrine.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: sudden production slowdowns - Peregrine route

Markus —

Since ~07:50 PST we've seen a sustained spike in p99 for the model route backing our /generate endpoint. Symptoms: higher tail latency (p99 ~7.3s vs normal ~0.9s), intermittent 503s for a subset of requests, and overall throughput drop (~35%). We started seeing queueing on our end (requests piling up client-side).

Logs attached (peregrine_error_snapshot_20261210.json) and a short sample of failed request ids. Can you confirm if there was a config change or rollout? This is customer-impacting — users on our platform are timing out. We need an immediate mitigation plan and ETA.

-Michael
Ops Lead, Peregrine Financial

Attachments: peregrine_error_snapshot_20261210.json (application/json, 48KB)

Michael — thanks for the heads up and the snapshot. We're on it. Initial ack: no intentional rollout from our side in the last 24h.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- Triage with SRE (Evelyn) to confirm whether queueing/backpressure is occuring in the serving cluster.
- If we see concurrency caps tripping for your route, we can raise the per-route cap and spin a burst pool.
- We'll correlate the request ids you sent with our traces — please let us know any replay ids if available.

I'll send a short mitigation plan within 20 minutes and keep you updated every 30.

-Markus

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: quick triage - Peregrine route

Internal triage (observed at 09:25 PST):
- Cluster: rwd-serving-prod-us-west-2, host group rwd-gpu-3.
- Symptom: incoming request queue depth on route "peregrine-main-v1" increased from median 12 -> 186 over ~25m. Backpressure activated; per-route concurrency cap at 64 is hitting and excess requests are being queued.
- RTT breakdown: cache hit ratio for prefix cache dropped (cache-miss heavy), leading to many cold KV-cache requests and long-sequence runs, which are more expensive on kernels. This increases per-request service time and amplifies queueing.

Mitigations proposed (hot):
1) Temporarily bump route concurrency cap from 64 -> 200 for "peregrine-main-v1".
2) Create a burst pool (rwd-burst-12) and route 30% of traffic to it for 10-20 minutes.
3) Enable aggressive KV-prefetch for your common prefixes (best-effort) — requires confirmation from customer side if they can avoid large one-off prompts.

I captured diagnostics (diagnostics_rwd-gpu-3-09-28.log) and a queue dump (queue_dump_20261210.txt). If you approve, I'll run the cap bump now (will take ~120s to take effect).

-Evelyn
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: diagnostics_rwd-gpu-3-09-28.log (text, 136KB); queue_dump_20261210.txt (text, 28KB)

Michael — quick update and immediate plan: we see queueing/backpressure and a cache-miss pattern driving long-sequence runs. Proposed mitigation (executing now if you approve):
- Raise per-route concurrency cap to 200 (expected immediate effect in ~2 minutes).
- Route a temporary burst pool with warm KV caches; we'll route ~30% of traffic there while we stabilize.
- We recommend you pause any heavy batched or non-interactive jobs for the next 30 minutes if possible.

We expect to see p99 drop within 5-15 minutes after the cap bump and burst routing. We'll monitor and share live dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/monitoring/peregrine-route-95

Do you approve the cap bump and temporary routing?

-Markus

From: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T17:42:00-08:00
Subject: Exec brief: Peregrine incident summary and ask

Jonas / Rishi — FYI and rapid decision requested. Summary of today's incident (timeline compressed):
- 07:50 PST: Peregrine reports elevated p99 and 503s.
- 09:25 PST: SRE triage found request queueing on hostgroup rwd-gpu-3 due to a sudden drop in prefix cache hit ratio; per-route concurrency cap (64) was tripping and creating backlog.
- 09:40 PST: We bumped per-route cap to 200 and routed ~30% traffic to a warm burst pool. Observable p99 decreased from ~7.3s -> ~1.2s over 12 minutes and error rate fell to baseline.
- Artifacts: diagnostics_rwd-gpu-3-09-28.log, queue_dump_20261210.txt, and the customer snapshot were collected and stored.

Root cause hypothesis: high variance in request surface caused widespread prefix cache misses that induced long-sequence executions; concurrency caps amplified queueing. Not seeing a rollout that would explain the change — candidate external drivers (customer batching changes) under review.

Actions taken: mitigation (cap bump + burst pool), collected traces and queue dumps, paused batch jobs per customer request, and committed to producing RCA within 72 hours.

Asks:
1) Executive sign-off on proposed commercial goodwill (recommend 10% usage credit for the impacted window).
2) Permission to publish a short joint customer-facing note if Peregrine's legal/comms request it.
3) If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute post-incident sync with Peregrine and include R&D to discuss model-side mitigations.

I'll circulate the full incident timeline and preliminary RCA once Evelyn and the tracing team finish correlation.

-Markus
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
